name: Generalized Morphea

criteria.description: Presence of multiple indurated plaques of skin thickening involving two or more body regions
No clinical or laboratory evidence of systemic sclerosis or internal organ involvement
Skin biopsy showing thickened collagen bundles with dermal fibrosis and absence of vasculitis
Presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) may be supportive but not diagnostic

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Multiple indurated plaques involving two or more body regions without systemic involvement, supported by histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by biopsy; systemic sclerosis must be excluded

pathognomonic.symptomName: Skin thickening with ivory or waxy appearance

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Mild joint stiffness adjacent to plaques

occasional.symptomName: Limited joint contractures near affected skin

rare.notes: Rare in generalized morphea, more typical of systemic sclerosis

laboratory: Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in 30-50% of cases
Normal systemic sclerosis-specific autoantibodies (e.g., anti-Scl-70 negative)
Normal inflammatory markers or mild elevation
imaging: MRI may show dermal and subcutaneous thickening
Ultrasound can detect skin and subcutaneous tissue fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating thickened collagen bundles and dermal fibrosis without vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly affects genital and perianal skin
White, atrophic plaques with epidermal thinning
Rapid onset of skin induration with fascial involvement
Absence of multiple plaques over large body areas

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms such as dyspnea or dysphagia
Rapid progression of skin thickening beyond plaques
references: Mertens JS et al. Localized scleroderma: clinical spectrum and therapeutic update. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Fett N, Werth VP. Update on morphea: part I. Epidemiology, clinical presentation, and pathogenesis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2011.
Kreuter A et al. Morphea: an update on pathogenesis and treatment. Am J Clin Dermatol. 2012.
